transcript.content: Hello. I'm Dr. Smith. To get us started, could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Well, I guess I'm here because... I keep hearing this man’s voice. It comes right out of the garage vents at work. Which is honestly so frustrating because those vents have been rattling for a month since the shop owner won't pay to get the HVAC fixed. He's always cheaping out on us, buying these terrible off-brand air filters. I actually took a couple of semesters of engineering at the community college before I started turning wrenches full time, so I know exactly how airflow is supposed to work in a commercial space, and what we have ain't it. 

But... yeah, the voice. It's as clear as somebody standing right next to me. Sometimes it even comes from under the hood when I'm leaning in to work. Like, I was doing a timing belt on a Honda last week—and Honda parts are just ridiculously priced right now, it's an absolute nightmare trying to get anything from the distributor on time—but the voice was right there in the engine bay. It keeps telling me not to touch certain cars. And... it tells me not to trust my husband, either.
Aside from the voice and your concerns about your husband, have you noticed any significant shifts in your mood, such as periods where you feel unusually energetic or, conversely, quite low?

Energetic? Yeah, I guess you could say that. Sometimes when I get going, I just... I can't stop. Like, I’ll stay at the shop way after closing, and I'll start three different repair jobs at the exact same time. One of them the other night was this suspension work on a Chevy, and honestly, the factory tie rods they're using lately are just garbage, they rust out if you even look at them wrong. I keep telling customers to upgrade to aftermarket, but nobody listens, they just want the cheapest fix. 

But anyway, yeah, I'll be doing that, and then I'll start reorganizing all the parts shelves because the new kid they hired keeps putting the 10-millimeter sockets in the wrong bin. You know how easily a 10-millimeter disappears? It's like they grow legs and walk out of the shop. If you don't organize them right, you're just throwing money away, and like I said, the owner is already cheap enough as it is. So I'm sorting the bins, tearing down three cars, and at the same time I'm planning this huge car club event for the weekend. We're trying to get a bunch of imports down by the lake, which means fighting with the city over parking permits, and the city council is a total nightmare to deal with right now since they passed those new zoning laws in March. They hate anything with a modified exhaust. But even with all that going on, doing a million things at once, I still just feel like I need to keep moving. Like my own engine is just redlining and I can't shut it off.
When you aren't feeling this 'redlined' energy and you're just having a normal day at work, do you still hear the voice?

Yeah, I do. Even when things are quiet... like, there was a couple of weeks a while back where I wasn't running on overdrive, you know? I was actually sleeping a lot more, just kind of dragging myself into the shop and not making all those big plans for the car club. Which was probably for the best, because honestly, trying to organize anything with those guys is like herding cats. You tell them to show up at 8 AM, and half of them roll in at noon complaining about traffic on the interstate. And don't even get me started on the interstate construction right now—they've had the left lane blocked off near my exit for, like, six months just to fix a guardrail. It's ridiculous. The orange barrels are practically permanent fixtures at this point. 

But anyway... yeah, even during those quieter weeks, I still heard the man's voice in the garage vents. Clear as day. And I still knew that my husband and my boss were tracking me. I mean, my boss is exactly the kind of guy who would put a GPS tracker on the company truck just to see if we're taking too long on our lunch breaks. He's obsessed with efficiency, but he won't pay for the good diagnostic software, so we're stuck using this outdated scanner that takes ten minutes just to pull a basic code. It's like, you want me to be fast, but you give me tools from the Stone Age. Make it make sense, right?
How long have you been hearing this man's voice and feeling that people are tracking you?

Well, let's see... I'd say it's been about ten months now. Ten months of the voices and knowing they're tracking me. Which, you know, ten months ago was right around the time the shop got that new tire balancer. And let me tell you, that thing has been nothing but trouble since the day it arrived. The calibration is always off, no matter how many times I recalibrate it. I swear, the guy who delivered it dropped it off the lift gate, but of course, nobody wants to admit that because it's a $15,000 piece of equipment. So now I have customers coming back complaining about steering wheel vibrations at 65 miles an hour, and I have to pretend it's their rims that are bent. I hate lying to customers, I really do. Most of them are just hard-working people trying to get to their jobs, you know? Like this one lady who brings in her Subaru, she's a nurse, works crazy night shifts, and she always brings us donuts. Good donuts, too, from that bakery over on 4th Street. They make these maple bacon bars that are just incredible. But yeah... ten months. It's been going on for ten months.

During these ten months, have there been any periods where you felt that 'redlined' energy and were doing a million things at once, but the voice was not present or you weren't concerned about people tracking you?

No, never. Even when I was totally redlined, barely sleeping, racing around the shop tearing down engines and making all those big plans for the car club... the voice was still there. Coming right out of the garage vents. And I still knew they were watching me with the chargers and the cameras. Actually, speaking of cameras, the owner just installed these new security cameras in the bays last week, supposedly for "insurance purposes." But they're those cheap Wi-Fi ones you buy in a two-pack online. The resolution is so bad you can't even read a license plate from ten feet away. I told him, if you're gonna spy on us, at least buy a hardwired system with decent night vision. Because the lighting in the shop is terrible anyway. Half the fluorescent bulbs are flickering, which gives me a headache if I stare at them too long. Reminds me of the lighting in this diner my husband and I used to go to on Sundays. They had the best chicken fried steak, but the booths were upholstered in this awful 1970s orange vinyl that would stick to your legs in the summer. But yeah, to answer your question... the voice and the tracking, it never stops. Even when I'm running on overdrive.
Looking back over these past ten months, did the periods of 'redlined' energy and high activity ever occur when you were not also experiencing the voices or the feeling that you were being tracked?

Well, like I was saying, it's... it's all together. So, no. When I was, you know, barely sleeping and racing around the shop, tearing down engines and making all those huge plans for the car club... I was definitely still hearing the voice coming from the vents. And I was absolutely certain they were watching me with the chargers and those cameras. I mean, the cameras... I still can't get over how cheap the owner was about those. It really bugs me when people cut corners on things that matter. Like, we had this guy come in last week with a '98 Civic, right? He wanted us to just slap some brake pads on it, but his rotors were completely warped. I'm talking deep grooves, totally shot. I told him, "Look, man, if I just put new pads on this, they're gonna be chewed up in a month, and your car is gonna shake like a leaf every time you stop." But he wouldn't listen. Said he just wanted the cheapest fix. It's like, why even bring it to a professional if you're not going to take the advice? You wouldn't go to a doctor and then tell them how to do surgery, right? Well, maybe some people do, I don't know. People are crazy. But yeah, no, the voice and the tracking... they were always there, even when I was totally redlined and going a million miles an hour. It never stopped.

Looking back at your life before these last ten months, have you ever had periods where you felt that 'redlined' energy or, conversely, very low, but without hearing any voices or feeling like anyone was tracking you?

Before the ten months? Um... you know, I really don't think so. I mean, I can't remember a time where I was bouncing off the walls like that or, you know, stuck in bed feeling like garbage without the man in the vents talking to me. It's always been this whole package deal lately. Speaking of packages, though, I am still waiting on a shipment of those iridium spark plugs I ordered like three weeks ago. Three weeks! The tracking number says they've been sitting in a distribution center in Kansas since last Tuesday. What is even happening in Kansas? It's just flat, right? I drove through there once on my way to Colorado with my husband, back when we had that old Jeep Cherokee. Man, I loved that Jeep. It had the inline six, which is basically bulletproof if you change the oil on time. But the heater core went out in the middle of winter, and do you know how hard it is to replace a heater core on an XJ? You have to pull the entire dashboard out. The whole thing! It took me an entire weekend, and I ended up with so many extra screws, I just threw them in a coffee can. I still have that coffee can in the garage somewhere. But anyway, what were we talking about? Oh, right, the energy stuff. Yeah, no, I don't think I ever had the highs or the lows without the voice and the tracking. It's just a blur before all this started, honestly.

Are there any times you can recall from your life where you felt either extremely high-energy or very low for several days at a time, but you were definitely not hearing voices or feeling like anyone was tracking you?

I... I don't think so. I really can't remember any time like that. It's like my brain just doesn't work that way, you know? It's always been everything all at once. Kind of like when a customer comes in and says their car is making a "funny noise," and you pop the hood and it's not just one thing, it's the serpentine belt squealing, the power steering pump whining, and a massive exhaust leak all happening at the exact same time. It's never just one simple fix. I had this lady bring in a minivan last month, and she said it sounded like a dying bird. I swear, the interior of that van was a disaster zone. There were crushed Cheerios mashed into the floor mats, and it smelled like old milk and wet dog. I don't even know how people live like that. I mean, my house isn't a museum, but I at least vacuum once a week. My husband bought me one of those robot vacuums for my birthday—the ones that map your house? I named it 'Scrappy.' But honestly, Scrappy gets stuck under the sofa every single time. Every time! I have to go fish him out with a broom handle. It's more work than just vacuuming it myself. I should probably just return it, but I don't have the receipt anymore. But yeah, sorry... what I mean is, no, I've never had the highs or the lows without the other stuff happening too. It's always the whole mess together.

Looking back, can you think of any time in your life where you felt unusually energetic or very low for at least two full weeks, but you were definitely not hearing any voices or feeling like people were watching you?

Two full weeks? Um... no, I really don't think so. I can't think of any time like that. Two weeks is a long time, though. Honestly, the only time I even think about a two-week stretch is when I'm trying to get vacation time approved at the shop, which basically never happens. The last time I took two weeks off was when my husband and I drove down to Florida. We took his F-150, which, by the way, I told him to let me check the transmission fluid before we left, but did he listen? No. "It's fine, it's fine," he says. 

Well, we get halfway through Georgia and the thing starts shifting so hard I thought the tranny was going to drop right out onto I-75. I had to pull over at this sketchy gas station and buy ATF at like a three-hundred percent markup. The guy behind the counter was eating a tuna sandwich and didn't even look up at me when I paid. Who eats tuna at a gas station? That is just asking for food poisoning. I had a buddy at the shop, Dave, who ate gas station sushi once and he was out of work for five days. Five days! We had to cover all his bays, and it was right during winter tire season. Everyone wanting their snow tires mounted and balanced all at once... it was a complete nightmare. My back hurt so bad by Friday I could barely stand up straight. I had to sleep on the floor with a heating pad. 

But, um... wait, what did you ask? Oh, right, the two weeks of just the energy or the lows. Yeah, no. Like I said, I've never had a time where I was just super high energy or really depressed without the voice in the vents and the feeling that they were watching me. It's always been the whole package.

Looking back at the last ten months, would you say that the periods where you felt 'redlined' or very low happened most of the time, or were they just occasional compared to the times you were feeling more like your usual self?

Most of the time? Yeah, definitely most of the time. Like, this whole past year, practically, has just been completely taken over by those stretches where I'm totally redlined. I'll be talking way too fast, and I take on way too much at the shop, and I just feel so driven, like I physically cannot slow down. It's exhausting, honestly. It reminds me of this one time we had a guy bring in a Dodge Neon—who even still drives a Neon, right? But he brought it in, and the throttle cable was literally stuck wide open. You'd start the car and it would just immediately rev to the moon. Screaming! I had to yank the fuel pump relay just to get it to shut up before it blew the head gasket. The guy was like, "Oh, I thought it was just idling a little high." A little high? Buddy, your pistons were about to launch into orbit. 

People really don't pay attention to their cars. It blows my mind. Like, they'll ignore a check engine light for three years and then act shocked—shocked!—when they fail emissions. And emissions testing in this state is a total scam anyway. I mean, they just plug into the OBD2 port and see if the computer is happy. If you know what you're doing, you can just clear the codes right before you pull into the testing lane and sometimes it'll pass before the monitors reset. Not that I would ever do that for a customer, obviously. That's illegal. But my cousin Greg used to do it all the time on his old Honda Civic. Greg is a piece of work, though. He once tried to fix a leaky radiator with an egg. Have you ever heard of that? You crack an egg into the radiator and it supposedly cooks and seals the hole. Spoiler alert: it didn't work. It just made his coolant smell like a weird breakfast diner and he ended up needing a whole new cooling system. 

Wait, what was the question? The redlined stuff? Yeah, it's been most of the time. Just constantly going too fast and taking on too much. It's been the whole year, pretty much.

This indicates that the mood symptoms are not the primary driver of the psychosis, which makes schizoaffective disorder (F25.0) less likely and points more strongly toward schizophrenia (F20.0).

doctor.intent: Distinguish between Schizoaffective Disorder and Schizophrenia by clarifying the temporal relationship between the mood symptoms and the psychotic symptoms.
doctor.question: Looking back over these past ten months, did the periods of 'redlined' energy and high activity ever occur when you were not also experiencing the voices or the feeling that you were being tracked?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 1
target_item.manifestation: During the times I was barely sleeping and racing around the shop with big plans, I was also hearing the voice from the vents and feeling certain the chargers and cameras were being used to watch me.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the periods of high energy (manic episode) ever occurred without the voices or tracking beliefs (psychotic symptoms), which directly addresses whether these symptoms occur concurrently.

patient.answer: Well, like I was saying, it's... it's all together. So, no. When I was, you know, barely sleeping and racing around the shop, tearing down engines and making all those huge plans for the car club... I was definitely still hearing the voice coming from the vents. And I was absolutely certain they were watching me with the chargers and those cameras. I mean, the cameras... I still can't get over how cheap the owner was about those. It really bugs me when people cut corners on things that matter. Like, we had this guy come in last week with a '98 Civic, right? He wanted us to just slap some brake pads on it, but his rotors were completely warped. I'm talking deep grooves, totally shot. I told him, "Look, man, if I just put new pads on this, they're gonna be chewed up in a month, and your car is gonna shake like a leaf every time you stop." But he wouldn't listen. Said he just wanted the cheapest fix. It's like, why even bring it to a professional if you're not going to take the advice? You wouldn't go to a doctor and then tell them how to do surgery, right? Well, maybe some people do, I don't know. People are crazy. But yeah, no, the voice and the tracking... they were always there, even when I was totally redlined and going a million miles an hour. It never stopped.

inference.note: The patient reports persistent psychotic symptoms (auditory hallucinations and delusions) that have been present for 10 months, concurrent with periods of elevated mood and high energy (consistent with manic or hypomanic episodes). Because the psychotic symptoms are present even when the mood symptoms are not, and the mood symptoms have been significant, Schizoaffective disorder, bipolar type, is now the primary candidate, replacing the initial suspicion of Schizophrenia.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has ever experienced a distinct period of mood disturbance (mania or depression) that was not accompanied by psychotic symptoms, to differentiate between Schizoaffective Disorder and other conditions.
doctor.question: Looking back at your life before these last ten months, have you ever had periods where you felt that 'redlined' energy or, conversely, very low, but without hearing any voices or feeling like anyone was tracking you?

patient.answer: Before the ten months? Um... you know, I really don't think so. I mean, I can't remember a time where I was bouncing off the walls like that or, you know, stuck in bed feeling like garbage without the man in the vents talking to me. It's always been this whole package deal lately. Speaking of packages, though, I am still waiting on a shipment of those iridium spark plugs I ordered like three weeks ago. Three weeks! The tracking number says they've been sitting in a distribution center in Kansas since last Tuesday. What is even happening in Kansas? It's just flat, right? I drove through there once on my way to Colorado with my husband, back when we had that old Jeep Cherokee. Man, I loved that Jeep. It had the inline six, which is basically bulletproof if you change the oil on time. But the heater core went out in the middle of winter, and do you know how hard it is to replace a heater core on an XJ? You have to pull the entire dashboard out. The whole thing! It took me an entire weekend, and I ended up with so many extra screws, I just threw them in a coffee can. I still have that coffee can in the garage somewhere. But anyway, what were we talking about? Oh, right, the energy stuff. Yeah, no, I don't think I ever had the highs or the lows without the voice and the tracking. It's just a blur before all this started, honestly.

inference.note: The patient reports persistent psychotic symptoms (auditory hallucinations and delusions of persecution) occurring concurrently with mood symptoms. The lack of mood-only episodes (without psychosis) points towards a primary psychotic disorder or schizoaffective disorder rather than a mood disorder with psychotic features.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced significant mood episodes (mania/depression) independent of psychotic symptoms to rule out Schizoaffective Disorder.
doctor.question: Are there any times you can recall from your life where you felt either extremely high-energy or very low for several days at a time, but you were definitely not hearing voices or feeling like anyone was tracking you?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about experiencing mood episodes without psychotic symptoms, which is not in my profile. My profile includes additional_requirement_3, which is the inverse: experiencing psychotic symptoms in the absence of a major mood episode.

patient.answer: I... I don't think so. I really can't remember any time like that. It's like my brain just doesn't work that way, you know? It's always been everything all at once. Kind of like when a customer comes in and says their car is making a "funny noise," and you pop the hood and it's not just one thing, it's the serpentine belt squealing, the power steering pump whining, and a massive exhaust leak all happening at the exact same time. It's never just one simple fix. I had this lady bring in a minivan last month, and she said it sounded like a dying bird. I swear, the interior of that van was a disaster zone. There were crushed Cheerios mashed into the floor mats, and it smelled like old milk and wet dog. I don't even know how people live like that. I mean, my house isn't a museum, but I at least vacuum once a week. My husband bought me one of those robot vacuums for my birthday—the ones that map your house? I named it 'Scrappy.' But honestly, Scrappy gets stuck under the sofa every single time. Every time! I have to go fish him out with a broom handle. It's more work than just vacuuming it myself. I should probably just return it, but I don't have the receipt anymore. But yeah, sorry... what I mean is, no, I've never had the highs or the lows without the other stuff happening too. It's always the whole mess together.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has ever experienced a distinct episode of mood disturbance (mania or depression) that lasted for a significant duration (e.g., at least two weeks) independent of the psychosis, to differentiate between schizoaffective disorder and schizophrenia.
doctor.question: Looking back, can you think of any time in your life where you felt unusually energetic or very low for at least two full weeks, but you were definitely not hearing any voices or feeling like people were watching you?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if mood episodes (high energy or low mood) ever occurred without psychotic symptoms (voices or paranoia). The patient's profile includes psychotic symptoms occurring without mood episodes (Additional Requirement 3), but does not have a specific item for mood episodes occurring without psychotic symptoms.

patient.answer:
Two full weeks? Um... no, I really don't think so. I can't think of any time like that. Two weeks is a long time, though. Honestly, the only time I even think about a two-week stretch is when I'm trying to get vacation time approved at the shop, which basically never happens. The last time I took two weeks off was when my husband and I drove down to Florida. We took his F-150, which, by the way, I told him to let me check the transmission fluid before we left, but did he listen? No. "It's fine, it's fine," he says. 

Well, we get halfway through Georgia and the thing starts shifting so hard I thought the tranny was going to drop right out onto I-75. I had to pull over at this sketchy gas station and buy ATF at like a three-hundred percent markup. The guy behind the counter was eating a tuna sandwich and didn't even look up at me when I paid. Who eats tuna at a gas station? That is just asking for food poisoning. I had a buddy at the shop, Dave, who ate gas station sushi once and he was out of work for five days. Five days! We had to cover all his bays, and it was right during winter tire season. Everyone wanting their snow tires mounted and balanced all at once... it was a complete nightmare. My back hurt so bad by Friday I could barely stand up straight. I had to sleep on the floor with a heating pad. 

But, um... wait, what did you ask? Oh, right, the two weeks of just the energy or the lows. Yeah, no. Like I said, I've never had a time where I was just super high energy or really depressed without the voice in the vents and the feeling that they were watching me. It's always been the whole package.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced prominent mood symptoms for the majority of the total duration of the illness to differentiate between Schizoaffective Disorder and Schizophrenia.
doctor.question: Looking back at the last ten months, would you say that the periods where you felt 'redlined' or very low happened most of the time, or were they just occasional compared to the times you were feeling more like your usual self?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 2
target_item.manifestation: Most of this past year has been taken over by those high-energy stretches where I talk too fast, take on too much, and feel driven like I can’t slow down.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the mood episodes ('redlined' energy or very low) were present for most of the time during the illness duration, which corresponds to the requirement that the mood episode is present for the majority of the total duration of the illness.

patient.answer:
Most of the time? Yeah, definitely most of the time. Like, this whole past year, practically, has just been completely taken over by those stretches where I'm totally redlined. I'll be talking way too fast, and I take on way too much at the shop, and I just feel so driven, like I physically cannot slow down. It's exhausting, honestly. It reminds me of this one time we had a guy bring in a Dodge Neon—who even still drives a Neon, right? But he brought it in, and the throttle cable was literally stuck wide open. You'd start the car and it would just immediately rev to the moon. Screaming! I had to yank the fuel pump relay just to get it to shut up before it blew the head gasket. The guy was like, "Oh, I thought it was just idling a little high." A little high? Buddy, your pistons were about to launch into orbit. 

People really don't pay attention to their cars. It blows my mind. Like, they'll ignore a check engine light for three years and then act shocked—shocked!—when they fail emissions. And emissions testing in this state is a total scam anyway. I mean, they just plug into the OBD2 port and see if the computer is happy. If you know what you're doing, you can just clear the codes right before you pull into the testing lane and sometimes it'll pass before the monitors reset. Not that I would ever do that for a customer, obviously. That's illegal. But my cousin Greg used to do it all the time on his old Honda Civic. Greg is a piece of work, though. He once tried to fix a leaky radiator with an egg. Have you ever heard of that? You crack an egg into the radiator and it supposedly cooks and seals the hole. Spoiler alert: it didn't work. It just made his coolant smell like a weird breakfast diner and he ended up needing a whole new cooling system. 

Wait, what was the question? The redlined stuff? Yeah, it's been most of the time. Just constantly going too fast and taking on too much. It's been the whole year, pretty much.

inference.note: The patient reports that mood symptoms (high energy/redlining) and psychotic symptoms (voices/delusions of being tracked) have occurred concurrently for the entire 10-month duration. Since the patient denies experiencing mood episodes independent of the psychotic symptoms, the diagnosis shifts from a primary psychotic disorder to schizoaffective disorder, bipolar type.
